report.source_text: Patient tested positive for COVID-19 by real-time reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test.

clinician.final_diagnosis: parainfectious type of optic neuritis following COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A previously healthy 22-year-old woman presented with acute onset blurring of vision and an absolute inferior visual field scotoma in the right eye 4 days prior, following recent febrile illness and known exposure to COVID-19. Ophthalmologic examination revealed 20/25 vision OD, relative afferent pupillary defect OD, and inferior altitudinal field defect OD. Fundoscopy showed optic disc margin blurring with vessel tortuosity. ONH-OCT demonstrated increased retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in superior, inferior, and nasal quadrants OD. Brain and spine MRI with contrast and CT of brain and orbit were normal, excluding demyelinating or other intracranial lesions. Neurological exam was normal, and VEP testing was not reported. Lab tests showed inflammatory markers consistent with recent infection, and RT-PCR confirmed COVID-19 infection. Clinical and diagnostic findings collectively support acute right optic neuritis as a parainfectious phenomenon following COVID-19 infection.
